D1.evidenceQuote: the Solendra Core development team successfully activates the 'Aurora' hard fork
D1.reasoning: The outcome is produced by the coordinated action of a development organization and validator set.

D2.evidenceQuote: targeted for mid-November 2026 per Solendra Improvement Proposal SIP-47
D2.reasoning: Much of the process is public, but readiness and postponement decisions are known to the core team and insiders before any announcement — dozens of people.

D3.evidenceQuote: a supermajority of Solendra mainnet validators
D3.reasoning: Developers and validator operators face no clear trading constraint; any foundation policies plausibly do not reach this venue.

D4.evidenceQuote: as measured by the protocol's own on-chain signaling mechanism
D4.reasoning: Activation is observable on-chain by everyone at once, on a roughly known schedule.

D5.evidenceQuote: formally postponed past November 30, 2026 by a published Solendra Core announcement
D5.reasoning: A small core group can time the outcome — announcing a postponement manufactures a NO resolution.
